[Northgate Facilities Maintenance Chat - #zone-c-shipping]

Dana Osei, 2026-05-18 09:14
something's off with A-142's brakes today. getting a grinding noise when I brake hard, and the pedal feels spongy, like it's got more travel than usual before it actually grabs. noticed it a couple times this morning moving pallets near the shipping doors.

Dana Osei, 2026-05-18 09:15
it's still stopping, just doesn't feel right. wasn't like this last week. I know it had brake work done back in the spring so figured someone should take a look before it gets worse

Dana Osei, 2026-05-18 09:16
going to keep using it carefully for now but wanted to flag it early

asset_id,work_order,service_date,technician,description,status
A-142,FIS-4471,2026-04-06,Tobias Krantz,Brake pad replacement (front and rear) on customer-reported soft pedal feel. Old pads worn near minimum thickness. Bled and adjusted brake lines after install. Test-drove unit in yard, pedal firm and responsive after repair.,Completed

--- page 1 ---

NORTHGATE FACILITIES
Follow-Up Equipment Inspection Report

Asset: A-142 (Talbrook TF-40 electric forklift)
Location: Zone C - Shipping
Inspection Date: 2026-05-21
Inspector: Lena Fischer, Northgate Facilities

Purpose: Follow-up inspection prompted by operator-reported brake grinding
noise and spongy pedal feel (reported 2026-05-18).

Background:
Unit had a full front and rear brake pad replacement performed by Ferrow
Industrial Services on 2026-04-06 (work order FIS-4471) following a
similar soft-pedal complaint at that time. This inspection is intended to
determine whether the current complaint represents a recurrence or a
separate issue.

--- page 2 ---

Findings:

Brake pedal travel is noticeably longer than spec before engagement,
consistent with the operator's description. Some grinding is audible
during hard braking, most pronounced at low speed. Visual inspection of
the brake assembly shows the recently replaced pads are wearing unevenly
- more material loss on the inboard side than expected for six weeks of
service. There is also a small amount of fluid weeping visible at a
fitting on the hydraulic brake line near the left rear wheel, not enough
to call it an active leak yet, but enough to note.

Given that this is the second brake complaint on this unit in under two
months, and the pad wear pattern is not consistent with normal use, this
looks more like a recurring issue than an isolated one - possibly a
sticking caliper or a slow line leak causing uneven pad wear and reduced
pedal firmness. Recommend a more thorough diagnostic beyond a simple pad
swap.

--- page 3 ---

Recommendation:

Follow-up diagnostic and repair should be scheduled within 5 business
days (by 2026-05-26) given the safety-relevant nature of a braking
system and the recurrence pattern. Unit may continue in service in the
interim only with caution and should be pulled immediately if the
operator reports any loss of braking effectiveness, not just noise or
feel.

Inspector signature: Lena Fischer
Report filed: 2026-05-21

--- page 4 ---

[End of report]

[Northgate Facilities Maintenance Chat - #yard]

Owen Vasquez, 2026-06-02 14:37
need someone from maintenance NOW. was bringing A-142 up the yard ramp with a load and the brakes did not hold, it started rolling backward and I nearly rolled into the rack at the bottom before I got it stopped with the parking brake. that is not a "feels spongy" problem anymore, the brakes flat out did not hold on the incline

Owen Vasquez, 2026-06-02 14:39
I pulled it and parked it at the bottom of the ramp, not moving it again until someone looks at it. this could have gone a lot worse, there were people near the bottom of that ramp

Owen Vasquez, 2026-06-02 14:40
I know it had a follow-up flagged after the inspection a couple weeks back, this needs to jump the line

From: Priya Nandakumar <p.nandakumar@northgatedc.example>
To: maintenance@northgatedc.example; safety@northgatedc.example
Subject: URGENT - A-142 brake failure on yard ramp, requesting hold from service
Date: 2026-06-02

Team,

Escalating this immediately. This afternoon Owen Vasquez was operating
A-142 on the yard ramp with a load and reported that the brakes did not
hold, causing the unit to roll backward toward the storage rack at the
bottom before he was able to stop it using the parking brake. No injuries
and no contact, but this was close and it happened on an incline with
people working nearby.

This is not the first flag on this unit's brakes. For reference:

- 2026-04-06: brake pad replacement by Ferrow Industrial Services after a
  soft-pedal complaint.
- 2026-05-18: operator reported grinding and spongy pedal again.
- 2026-05-21: follow-up inspection found uneven pad wear and fluid
  weeping at a line fitting, recommended a full diagnostic within 5
  business days.
- 2026-06-02 (today): brake failure to hold on an incline under load.

Given the pattern and the severity of today's incident, I am formally
requesting that A-142 be held from service effective immediately, pending
a full review and sign-off before it goes back on the floor. Please do
not return this unit to service without that review regardless of any
quick fix that gets applied - I want the full history looked at, not
just today's symptom.

Owen has parked the unit at the bottom of the yard ramp. Please have
maintenance move it under power-off/tow only if it needs to be relocated.

Priya Nandakumar
Shift Supervisor, Northgate Distribution Center

Repair Update - Zone C / Yard

Asset: A-142 (Talbrook TF-40 electric forklift)
Date: 2026-06-03
Logged by: Marcus Ibe

Picking this one up per Priya's email yesterday. Towed A-142 in from the
bottom of the yard ramp this morning and got it into a bay in the
Maintenance area. Pulled the wheels to get a look at the brake assembly
before doing anything else.

Assigning this to myself for the full diagnostic Lena's report called
for. Not doing a quick turnaround on this one - given the ramp incident
and the repeat history I want to trace the hydraulic line fully and
check the caliper before anything gets reassembled. Ordered a replacement
caliper and line fitting kit in case that's what we're looking at, should
be in within a few days.

Status: A-142 is OUT OF SERVICE, tagged and locked out. Not to be
returned to the floor without sign-off per Priya's request. Awaiting
parts and a decision on scope of repair before proceeding further.
